AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MAY 18, 2021
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20, N-29-20, AND N-35-20, WHICH ALLOWS MEETINGS TO BE
VIDEOCONFERENCED WITHOUT PROVIDING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS
DURING A MEETING, EITHER SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685
DURING THE MEETING TO SPEAK ON AN ITEM. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED ON FIOS CHANNEL 32
OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3 OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-
agendas-393.
  5:15 PM
  VIDEOCONFERENCE
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Vice Mayor
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Ana Valencia, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Vice Mayor Ayala

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION
  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957(a): THREAT TO
  PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES – Consultation with the City Manager, Los Angeles County Sheriff
  representative, and other related City officials.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Vice Mayor Ayala

INVOCATION
  Richard Rojas
  Deputy City Manager

FLAG SALUTE
  Carina Montes
  Director of Human Resources

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to proclaim May as Older Americans Month in the City of Norwalk.

  II.  City Council to proclaim National Public Works Week as May 16 - 22, 2021 in the City of Norwalk.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Coast Plaza Vaccine Clinic Collaboration.

  3.  First Responders Appreciation Lunch Recap.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
   waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

  2.  MEETING MINUTES - Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of May 4,
  and 11, 2021. 825-04

  Minutes

  3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period April 4, – April 17, 2021,
  in the total amount of $877,784.83. 630

  Report

  4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period April
  29, - May 12, 2021, in the total amount of $2,412,290.83. 640

  Warrant Register

  5.  ORDINANCE NO. 21-1725 - AMENDING NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 1.13 RELATING
  TO HEARINGS CONTESTING ADMINISTRATIVE CITATIONS AND ADDING CHAPTER 2.18 –
  ESTABLISHING A HOUSING AND BUILDING LOCAL APPEALS BOARD - Staff recommends City
  Council accept for second reading and adopt Ordinance No. 21-1725, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  OF NORWALK ADDING A NEW CHAPTER 2.18 TO THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE
  ESTABLISHING A HOUSING AND BUILDING LOCAL APPEALS BOARD AND AMENDING
  NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 1.13 RELATING TO HEARINGS CONTESTING
  ADMINISTRATIVE CITATIONS. 240/616-06

  Report

  6.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT – PARKING MANAGEMENT SERVICES – Staff recommends City
  Council approve Amendment No. 8, extending the term of the agreement with Parking Concepts,
  Incorporated, for an additional one-year term beginning July 6, 2021; and authorize the City Manager
  to execute the amendment on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 920-04

  Report

  7.  CONFIRM EMERGENCY WORK AT 15603 WILDER AVENUE, 12323 ALONDRA BOULEVARD,
  CLARKDALE AVENUE AND SYCAMORE STREET, AND 13937 JERSEY AVENUE – Staff
  recommends City Council confirm the emergency service repair work at 15603 Wilder Avenue, 12323
  Alondra Boulevard, Clarkdale Avenue and Sycamore Street, and 13937 Jersey Avenue, completed by
  Precision Pipeline, Inc., in the amount of $23,765.78. 955

  Report

  8.  APPROVE IMPLEMENTATION AGREEMENT FOR IMPERIAL HIGHWAY COMPLETE STREET
  STUDY - Staff recommends City Council approve the Implementation Agreement with Gateway Cities
  Council of Governments for the Imperial Highway Complete Street Study in the amount of $11,491.37
  in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1015-04-01

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  9.  ADVISORY BODIES - Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

RESOLUTIONS

  10. RESOLUTION NO. 21-24 - APPROVING A NON-CONSUMPTIVE WATER USE PERMIT FOR
  GROUNDWATER CLEANUP IN THE CITY OF COMPTON AT THE DEMENNO-KERDOON SITE FOR
  WORLD OIL RECYCLING – Staff recommends City Council:
   a.  adopt Resolution No. 21-24, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK APPROVING A NON-CONSUMPTIVE WATER USE PERMIT FOR GROUNDWATER
  CLEANUP IN THE CITY OF COMPTON AT THE DEMENNO-KERDOON SITE FOR WORLD OIL
  RECYCLING; and

  b.  authorize the City Manager to execute an Agreement for Assignment of a Non-Consumptive Water
  Use Permit with Demenno-Kerdoon, dba World Oil Recycling, and any amendments, on behalf of
  the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1070-08

  Report

  11. RESOLUTION NO. 21-25 - BUDGET AMENDMENT AND AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO MEMORANDUM
  OF UNDERSTANDING TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A WATERSHED MANAGEMENT PROGRAM
  AND COORDINATED INTEGRATED MONITORING PROGRAM FOR THE LOWER SAN GABRIEL
  RIVER WATERSHED COMMITTEE - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 21-25, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK APPROVING AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO THE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING
  WITH GATEWAY WATER MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A
  WATERSHED MANAGEMENT PROGRAM AND COORDINATED INTEGRATED MONITORING
  PROGRAM FOR THE LOWER SAN GABRIEL RIVER WATERSHED COMMITTEE; AND
  AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2020/21 ADOPTED BUDGET TO
  APPROPRIATE AVAILABLE ENTERPRISE FUNDS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2020/21
  REQUIREMENTS UNDER THE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH GATEWAY
  WATER MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY, in the amount of $54,067.00; and

  b.  authorize the City Manager to execute the Amendment on behalf of the City, in a form approved by
  the City Attorney. 1070-10

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated May 13, 2021.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
